title.narrative: Kapit-Bisig Laban sa Kahirapan-Comprehensive and Integrated Delivery of Social Services (Kalahi-CIDSS) National Community-Driven Development Project

description.narrative:
The project will support the implementation of the government's KALAHI CIDSS- National Community-Driven Development Project (KC-NCDDP) to restore basic social services and rebuild communities affected by Typhoon Yolanda (international name: Haiyan).
The impact will be improved resiliency of poor communities to natural hazards. The outcome will be improved access to services and infrastructure for communities in affected provinces and their participation in more inclusive local disaster risk reduction and management planning, budgeting, and implementation.
The outputs are (i) community-driven development subprojects selected, implemented, and completed; (ii) institutional and organizational capacity strengthened; and (iii) program management and monitoring and evaluation systems enhanced.

description.narrative: Improved access to services and infrastructure for communities in affected provinces and their participation in more inclusive local disaster risk reduction and management planning, budgeting, and implementation

35% of households in covered municipalities reporting increased confidence to participate in community development by 2017 Progress/Status: Results of the household survey shows that 94.24% of the household respondents claimed having the confidence to participate in community development activities. Such figure is a also a bit over the baseline estimates of 94% - a salient 0.24 percentage-point increase. (Data from First Round Outcome Survey result only) Data Source: Midterm and end-line community and household surveys Baseline value:

45% of members from marginalized groups (indigenous peoples and women) in covered municipalities attend regular barangay (village) assemblies by 2017 Progress/Status: Of the total number of female-headed households surveyed, 74% claimed having participated in DILG mandated synchronized barangay assemblies in the past 12 months. Meanwhile, 75% of the IP households narrated the same where majority are from Luzon Island (80%). (Data from First Round Outcome Survey result only) Data Source: Midterm and end-line KC-NCDDP management information system data from barangay assembly meeting minutes and attendance complemented by specialized household surveys Baseline value:

900,000 households benefited by 2017 Progress/Status: Exceeded. 3,853,968 households are directly benefiting from 14,863 completed community sub-projects (ADB-Funded). Data Source: Midterm and end-line community and household surveys Baseline value: 0

Access to and utilization of basic services and infrastructure such as roads, education, health centers, and water in covered municipalities increased by 10% by 2017 Progress/Status: 5% decrease in time spent 58% increase in cost (dry season) 61% increase in cost (wet season) (Data from First Round Outcome Survey result only) Data Source: Midterm and end-line KC-NCDDP management information system data from barangay assembly meeting minutes and attendance complemented by specialized household surveys Baseline value: 0
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. CDD subprojects selected, implemented, and completed Indicator: 85% of completed subprojects in covered municipalities have satisfactory or better sustainability evaluation ratings by 2017 (baseline: 0% in 2013) Progress/Status: Target exceeded (99%)
11,150 (99%) out of the 11,300 SPs with reported sustainability evaluation (SE) results rated satisfactory or better. Data Source: Annual KC-NCDDP report from the subproject sustainability evaluation reports of barangays and municipalities Actual value:

Output: 1. CDD subprojects selected, implemented, and completed Indicator: 85% of completed subprojects meet basic financial standards based on finance and administration submanual by 2017 (baseline: 0% in 2013) Progress/Status: Target exceeded (100%). All completed sub-projects were able to meet basic financial standards in accordance to the KC-NCDDP Finance and Management Sub-manual. Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress report from community projects completion reports Actual value:

Output: 1. CDD subprojects selected, implemented, and completed Indicator: 85% of subprojects in covered municipalities completed in accordance with technical plans, schedule, and budget by 2017 (baseline: 0% in 2013) Progress/Status: Achieved 85.3%.
Out of the 11,669 ADB-funded sub-projects that were planned to be completed within 180 days, 70% (8,122) were completed within schedule; 86% (12,744) out of the 14,863 SPs were completed in accordance to technical plans based on SPCR while 100% of the subprojects were within budget. Allocating equal weights for each subproject indicator, the overall achievement for this KPI is 85.3%. Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress report from community projects completion reports Actual value:

Output: 2. Institutional and organizational capacity strengthened Indicator: 85% of covered municipalities have increased membership of people's and civil society organizations in local development councils and special bodies by 2017 Progress/Status: Target exceeded (100%. All 800 enrolled municipalities have MOA with DSWD that call to expand the membership of POs and CSOs in Municipal Development Council Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress reports from the municipal and barangay LGU reports Actual value:

Output: 1. CDD subprojects selected, implemented, and completed Indicator: 150 livelihood and economic support subprojects implemented and completed by 2017 Progress/Status: Below target. A total of 128 livelihood subprojects have been funded, of which 94 have been completed.
Reasons for not achieving 150 target by end of program are due to: · Timeline of implementation which affected utilization. The Grant Agreement between the Philippines and ADB was only entered into last March 21, 2016 while the budget for the implementation was transferred to DSWD account in August 2016. The delayed start and downloading of funds to regions resulted to a domino effect of other activities such as the delayed conduct of social preparations, provision of technical assistance, conduct of trainings and meetings with various stakeholders. · Multi-component subprojects. The communities and KC NCDDP Staff required longer time to prepare the necessary documents, package the proposal and comply with the RFR requirements since most of the sub-projects are multi-components and involve multi-stakeholders. Example of this include a sub-project with skills training, starter kit and infrastructure support. Activities and materials needed to be packaged within the approved procurement guidelines of NCDDP while the technical designs included the review of other agencies such as DA, BFAR, DOST and DTI.
While the Project was not able to reach 150 SPs, it has reached more than 150 communities since some of the sub-projects were implemented by multiple communities. Example of this are the 5 water systems in Tanauan which covers 21 barangays and the Construction of Artificial Reef and Fish Cage with Skills Training on Fish Production which involves 5 barangays. Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress report from community projects completion reports Actual value:

Output: 3. Program management and M&E systems enhanced Indicator: 100% of newly targeted 189 municipalities generate sex-disaggregated data by 2017 (baseline: 10% in 2009) Progress/Status: Achieved/target exceeded. A total of 273 new KC-NCDDP municipalities (Yolanda affected) are generating sex-disaggregated data using the CDD forms and database which require sex-disaggregation. Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress reports Actual value:

Output: 2. Institutional and organizational capacity strengthened Indicator: 50% of the leadership positions in community volunteer committees held by women by 2017 (baseline: 35% in 2012) Progress/Status: Target exceeded. 113,209 (60%) out of the 189,872 committee chairpersonships are held by women. Data Source: Quarterly KC- NCDDP progress reports Actual value:

Output: 1. CDD subprojects selected, implemented, and completed Indicator: 20%-30% of the paid jobs created by the project are held by women by 2017 (baseline: 3% for skilled and 5% for unskilled in 2013) Progress/Status: Achieved 21%.
76,774 women have been engaged in paid labor during sub-project implementation, comprising 21% of the total 371,341 workers. Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress report from community projects completion reports Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: 3%/5% Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: 3%/5% Target year: 2017 Target value: 20%-30%

Output: 2. Institutional and organizational capacity strengthened Indicator: At least 10 community volunteers per village trained in CDD, (including livelihood subproject preparation) by 2017, of which 50% are women Progress/Status: Target exceeded. 546,620* in 18,781 villages (or average of 29 CVs per village). (61% women)
*unique volunteers
546,620 community volunteers have been mobilized and been provided various trainings, of which 334,538 (61%) are women. Data Source: Quarterly KC- NCDDP progress reports Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2017 Target value: 10/50%

Output: 3. Program management and M&E systems enhanced Indicator: At least one study on effectiveness and impacts completed, including a review of gender equality dimensions and livelihood gains, by 2017 Progress/Status: The study on effectiveness and impacts is part of the Outcome Survey. Social Weather Stations was engaged to conduct Outcome Survey second round.
Study on livelihood gains included in the ADB thematic studies. Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress reports Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y

Output: 3. Program management and M&E systems enhanced Indicator: Gender action plan implemented by 2017 Progress/Status: Partially achieved. Most of the indicators were already achieved except for study on review of gender equality. Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress reports Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y

Output: 3. Program management and M&E systems enhanced Indicator: System for community requests for fund release fully operating by 2014 Progress/Status: Achieved/Completed.
E-RFR system installed and fully operational in all regions. Data Source: Quarterly KC-NCDDP progress reports Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2014 Target value: Y
